sources.fact: Spring 2026 is a January 2026 snapshot covering fixed availability, FWA, take-up, satellite and mobile evidence.
sources.guard: Snapshot or area coverage is not selected-address retail orderability.

sources.fact: The 2026 report records operator plans to the end of 2028 and distinguishes high-confidence plans.
sources.guard: Forward plans, including high-confidence plans, are not current activation or accepted orders.

sources.fact: The PND collection explains that reports supplement Connected Nations and are not comprehensive or definitive.
sources.guard: Do not treat operator-plan totals as complete property-level truth.

sources.fact: The coverage hub separates existing coverage, planned deployments, performance and checker products.
sources.guard: Keep product purpose and measurement level separate.

sources.fact: Infrastructure research lists annual and interim reports with distinct coverage and plan vintages.
sources.guard: Do not merge different report vintages without explicit epoch handling.

sources.fact: The checker uses operator-supplied predictions for a selected property.
sources.guard: Postcode or partial-area results must not be copied to every property.

sources.fact: USO is a request and eligibility assessment considering existing and planned service and cost.
sources.guard: Eligibility is not live service, order acceptance or installation.

sources.fact: The May 2026 OMR requests current and three-year planned gigabit coverage.
sources.guard: Supplier submissions are planning evidence, not delivery commitments.

sources.fact: The May review closed and submissions entered evaluation while outputs remained pending.
sources.guard: Closure and receipt are not assessed or published coverage.

sources.fact: The January review records a separate consultation and supplier-submission epoch.
sources.guard: Keep January and May review rounds separate.

sources.fact: January submissions were assessed before publication of outputs.
sources.guard: Submission, assessment and publication are different states.

sources.fact: The collection publishes dated monthly contract-level progress snapshots.
sources.guard: Contract progress is not selected-UPRN service availability.

sources.fact: The July snapshot notes initial-scope limits, ingestion lag and non-comparability with official statistics.
sources.guard: Lag or scope omission is not failed delivery or NO_DATA.

sources.fact: The May release records supplier resubmissions that revise administrative data.
sources.guard: Administrative revision is not a negative delivery event.

sources.fact: OS Places supports address, postcode, UPRN and spatial search but not unrestricted bulk querying.
sources.guard: Interactive API access does not establish bulk completeness.

sources.fact: The API separates Find, Postcode and UPRN verification from Nearest, BBOX, Radius and Polygon GeoSearch.
sources.guard: Spatial candidates are not exact identity matches.

sources.fact: The UPRN endpoint requires a valid identifier and returns dataset, epoch, last-update and CRS metadata.
sources.guard: Retain lifecycle and response metadata before binding service evidence.

sources.fact: BBOX has a one-square-kilometre limit and supports filters and paged results.
sources.guard: Tile deterministically and reach the terminal page before NO_DATA.

sources.fact: Radius uses a centre point, distance up to 1,000 metres and explicit CRS handling.
sources.guard: Proximity does not transfer the target property's status.

sources.fact: Polygon accepts GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon input and returns intersecting address candidates.
sources.guard: Intersection is not parcel containment or legal boundary proof.

sources.fact: Nearest returns the closest address within a maximum 1,000-metre search.
sources.guard: The nearest address is not necessarily the target address.

sources.fact: Linked Identifiers exposes identifier, identifier-type, feature-type and product-version endpoints.
sources.guard: Store namespace, feature type, relationship method and version.

sources.fact: ONS postcode products relate current and terminated postcodes to statistical geographies.
sources.guard: A postcode point or geography is not a property, parcel or service.

sources.fact: National Polygon Service links index polygons, title descriptors and Title Number-UPRN data under licence.
sources.guard: Index polygons and title links are indicative, not exact legal boundaries.

sources.fact: OS documents 4xx request errors, 429 rate limiting and 5xx service errors.
sources.guard: Technical HTTP states must never be stored as valid empty property results.

sources.fact: OS API access uses API projects, keys or OAuth credentials.
sources.guard: Authentication failure is an access state, not NO_DATA.

sources.fact: Requests above the allowed rate are rejected with 429 until the request rate falls.
sources.guard: 429 requires retry/backoff and cannot establish absence.

sources.fact: The technical specification defines OS Open UPRN structure, CRS, supply and currency.
sources.guard: Point identifiers are not parcel polygons or ownership records.

sources.fact: Release notes document product epochs, record counts, issues and enhancements.
sources.guard: Retain epoch and known-issue state before cross-release comparison.

sources.fact: OS Open UPRN is refreshed about every six weeks with AddressBase epoch dates.
sources.guard: An older epoch may be stale without implying property absence.

sources.fact: The product is available as a free download and refreshed on a six-weekly basis.
sources.guard: Supply availability does not itself verify a specific address lifecycle.

sources.fact: The feature type carries a UPRN and British National Grid point coordinates.
sources.guard: Coordinate presence supports location only, not building extent or title.

sources.fact: Product Version Information returns version context for identifier relationships.
sources.guard: Hold stale or unversioned relationships from authoritative binding.

sources.fact: OS Features API uses paged feature collections and common authentication, error and rate-limit controls.
sources.guard: A partial page is not a complete spatial result.

sources.fact: OS Downloads API exposes product metadata, package versions and download links.
sources.guard: Metadata discovery is not proof that bytes were downloaded and validated.

sources.fact: OS notes that Match and Cleanse is unsuitable for bulk processing and is being withdrawn.
sources.guard: Do not build new bulk completeness assumptions on an end-of-life API.

sources.fact: The guidance describes the licensed National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number-UPRN datasets.
sources.guard: Licence and access restrictions must remain explicit.

sources.fact: Title Number and UPRN Look Up links titles and UPRNs where a relationship is available.
sources.guard: No match is not proof of no title; one-to-many links require handling.

sources.fact: National Polygon Dataset publishes HMLR index polygons for England and Wales.
sources.guard: Indexing geometry is not guaranteed legal extent.

sources.fact: Title Descriptor carries title identifiers and estate, class and registration attributes.
sources.guard: Pending or missing attributes must not be converted to NO_DATA.

sources.fact: INSPIRE Index Polygons can locate registered-title index records but cannot establish exact title extent.
sources.guard: INSPIRE polygons are discovery evidence, not legal boundary proof.

sources.fact: INSPIRE data is updated monthly and each polygon has an HMLR INSPIRE identifier.
sources.guard: Monthly index geometry remains a subset and not all property evidence.

sources.fact: Index-map search can identify titles missing from ordinary register search and can confirm unregistered land.
sources.guard: A normal search miss is not sufficient to conclude no title.

sources.fact: NSUL and ONSUD allocate UPRNs to statistical and administrative geographies using point-in-polygon methods.
sources.guard: Geography allocation is not address identity, title or broadband evidence.

sources.fact: ONS explains postcode inclusion and six-weekly product updates with possible source-epoch limitations.
sources.guard: Postcode currency lag must not become property absence.

sources.fact: The 2026 catalogue lists May 2026 postcode products and March 2026 UPRN lookup epochs.
sources.guard: Catalogue presence and product epoch must be retained separately.

sources.fact: The 2025 PND report used January 2025 plans to the end of 2027.
sources.guard: Do not overwrite 2026 plans with an older plan vintage.

sources.fact: The 2023 report documents earlier projections and subsequent provider plan revisions.
sources.guard: Historical plan changes are revisions, not completed deployment evidence.
